title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this 'quatrième mouture' of Analysis situs, Grothendieck is axiomatising 'tame' geometric figures through two notions. A 'magasin' (store) is a set M of 'specimens' on a set of points L, with M ⊂ PP(L); it is closed under passing to sub-figures and contains the singletons {{x}}. An 'atelier' (workshop) is built on top of a magasin. The previous page records his decision that it is clearer to start from magasins and construct ateliers from them, rather than the reverse.

The page opens by finishing that remark. The atelier is to be presented as a game associated with a magasin, and one must check that the essential Props 1-5 hold in that setting.

Dated 27 (or 28) June 1986, the page then gives two definitions.

(1) Antifiltre. Let (𝓕, ≤) be a poset. An antifiltre is a subset 𝓕' ⊂ 𝓕 that is (a) down-closed (F ∈ 𝓕', G ≤ F ⇒ G ∈ 𝓕') and (b) closed under those binary joins that exist in 𝓕 (F, G ∈ 𝓕' and F∨G exists in 𝓕 ⇒ F∨G ∈ 𝓕'). In modern terms this is an order ideal of a partial join-semilattice, closed under existing finite joins: the order-dual of a filter, which explains the name.

(2) M-atelier. Given a magasin M, an M-atelier (the transcription's 'M-situation' should read 'M-atelier') is an antifiltre 𝓕 in the poset 𝓕_M of M-figures. It must contain the elementary figures X̃ (X ∈ M) and the empty figure.

NB. The emptiness condition is redundant when M ≠ ∅, because ∅ ≤ X̃ and 𝓕 is down-closed. The following are equivalent: (i) M = ∅; (ii) 𝓕 = {∅}; (iii) Card 𝓕 = 1. This is correct: if M = ∅ then 𝓕_M = {∅}. If 𝓕 = {∅}, no X̃ lies in 𝓕, so M = ∅. Card 𝓕 = 1 forces 𝓕 = {∅} because ∅ ∈ 𝓕.

He then begins to coin terminology: the atelier is called 'vide' in that case, though it is not quite empty, since it contains the empty figure.

The left margin restates the atelier axioms in set-theoretic form. (b) F, G ∈ 𝓕 and F∪G ∈ 𝓕_M ⇒ F∪G ∈ 𝓕 (the join in 𝓕_M is the union). (c) X̃ ∈ 𝓕 for all X ∈ M. (c') 𝓕 ≠ ∅, i.e. ∅ ∈ 𝓕. (c) and (c') are equivalent provided 𝓕 contains the figures ∐(M) (when M ≠ ∅).

Purpose: an atelier is a class of admissible figures, closed under refinement-downwards and under admissible unions. The next page abstracts this further: 𝓕 with relations ≤, ≪, etc.; sups exist; elementary figures are completely join-irreducible; every figure is the sup of the elementary figures (strata) below it. It also adds a stability axiom for filtered increasing families of refinements, needed for Prop. 4 (gluing of refinements). This is a step toward the axiomatics of 'géométrie modérée' announced in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence (i)⇔(ii)⇔(iii) and the redundancy of '∅ ∈ 𝓕' when M ≠ ∅ are both correct (they use that the empty figure is ≤ every X̃).
Minor terminological wobble: Grothendieck hesitates over calling the trivial atelier 'vide', since it contains the empty figure. This is the usual empty-versus-trivial issue, not an error.

ideas.what: Antifiltre: a down-closed subset of a poset that is closed under existing binary joins
ideas.modern_name: Order ideal (closed under existing finite joins), dual of a filter

ideas.what: M-atelier: an ideal of the poset of M-figures containing all elementary figures, i.e. an admissible class of 'tame' figures generated over a store of specimens
ideas.modern_name: Close in spirit to a structure of definable/tame sets (o-minimal structure), or an admissible family of stratified sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1984-86)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is announced in Esquisse §5; this specific axiomatics is unpublished

missed.claim: The 1986 Analysis situs notes contain an order-theoretic axiomatics of tame geometry: stores of specimens (magasins), ateliers as ideals in the poset of figures, and later abstract axioms with join-irreducible elementary figures. This is distinct from the model-theoretic o-minimal approach. This page itself contributes only the basic definitions; the substance lies in the surrounding pages.
missed.quote: Une M-atelier est par définition un antifiltre 𝓕 dans l'ens 𝓕_M des M-figures ... contenant les figures élémentaires X̃ (X∈M) et la figure vide
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible lattice/poset-theoretic foundation for tame topology, comparable to o-minimal structures. It is of interest mainly historically; this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary order-theoretic definitions (an antifiltre is a poset ideal) used to set up Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatics of tame figures. It is historically interesting as part of the tame-topology project, but nothing on this page would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit M un ingénieux' should read 'Soit M un magasin'. Likewise 'M est ingénieux vide' should read 'M est magasin vide' / 'l'atelier 𝓕 est vide'.
'Une M-situation' and 'la situation 𝓕' likely read 'M-atelier' and 'l'atelier 𝓕'; the crossed-out phrase is 'un atelier théorique'.
Opening line: 'que l'situation comme un jeu ad hoc : une ingénieuse' plausibly reads '... l'atelier comme un jeu associé : un magasin — et de vérifier les prop. essentielles prop 1 à prop 5 ...'.
'27 juin (ou plutôt, 28 juin ! (le ne sait plus...)' should read '... (on ne sait plus ...)'.
Margin (b): '... F∨G ... ⇒ F∪G∈𝓕' should read 'F,G ∈ 𝓕, F∪G ∈ 𝓕_M ⇒ F∪G ∈ 𝓕'. Margin (c) reads '∀X∈M, X̃∈𝓕', not 'x̃'. The margin heading is 'Magasin' / 'M≠∅'.
